html:
The Arrernte are an Aboriginal Australian people of Central Australia, in the MacDonnell Ranges and the country around Alice Springs, which they call Mparntwe. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language, with several dialects, is one of the best known in Central Australia.

Their neighbours were the Luritja to the west, the Anmatyerre and Alyawarre to the north and the Antakirinja to the south. Their country is laced with the tracks of ancestral beings of the Dreaming, such as the caterpillars whose story shapes the gaps and ridges around Alice Springs.

Contact came with the Overland Telegraph Line, which put a station at Alice Springs in 1872. In 1877 Lutheran missionaries founded Hermannsburg in Western Arrernte country. The anthropologists Baldwin Spencer and Francis Gillen published a famous study of the Arrernte in 1899. The painter Albert Namatjira, a Western Arrernte man, grew up at Hermannsburg.
